title: Wash your motorcycle safely
summary: Clean the bike without forcing water into bearings, connectors and the air intake.

steps.text: Wash when the engine and exhaust are cool. Plug the muffler opening with a rag.
Rinse with low-pressure water to lift loose dirt.
steps.caution: Don't aim a pressure washer at wheel bearings, the instrument panel, switches, electrical connectors or the CVT air intake.

steps.text: Wash from the top down with soapy water and the mitt, using the second bucket to rinse the mitt.
Scrub wheels and the lower body last with the brush so grit doesn't scratch the paint.
Rinse again, then dry with microfiber towels. Blow water out of switches and connectors if you have a blower.
Remove the muffler rag, start the engine and let it run for a few minutes to dry off.
Test the brakes at low speed before riding normally, and re-lube the chain on chain bikes.
steps.caution: Wet discs and soap residue reduce braking. Keep soap and polish off the discs.
